title: Downloads in incomplete get stuck there if they temporarily can't be moved to completed downloads folder
body:
Nicotine+ version:  3.3.10
Operating System/Distribution: Nixos

### Describe the bug
I had accidentally set permissions for the completed downloads such that nicotine+ couldn't access it. Downloads in the incomplete download folder finished, and I saw the error that it couldn't move them to the completed folder. I investigated, realized there was a permissions issue, and fixed the permissions issue with the completed downloads folder. But the finished downloads just stayed in the incomplete downloads folder (with their prepended bit `INCOMPLETEc6674bc98610fdff807dbb7ab405920a<original filename>` filename.

### Expected behavior
Once permissions are set properly for the completed downloads folder, the downloads should be moved from the incomplete downloads folder to the complete downloads folder (and placed in their proper subfolders, where appropriate). Or there should be a way to signal the app to try again to move them.

### Steps to reproduce the bug
Set permissions for the completed downloads folder such that the app's user doesn't have write access. Download something. Wait until it finishes. Fix the permissions issue (give the app's user write access). See the file remain in the incomplete downloads folder.

### Additional context
Screenshots, logs, stacktraces or relevant information.

title: Windows portable build blocks other GTK/Python applications (like Zim Wiki) from starting
body:
Nicotine+ version:  3.3.10 
Operating System/Distribution: Windows 7 x64 


### Describe the bug
When the portable version of Nicotine+ is running, it completely blocks other portable GTK/Python applications (such as Zim Wiki) from initializing their GUI.If Nicotine+ is started first, launching zim.exe results in a background process appearing in Task Manager, but no window is ever drawn. If Zim Wiki is started first, both applications work fine simultaneously.The issue seems to be caused by Nicotine+ aggressively hijacking the default GApplication local socket / D-Bus session bus on Windows, causing other GTK apps to mistake Nicotine+'s process for their own backend single-instance server.

### Expected behavior
Nicotine+ should isolate its GApplication ID and local socket communication so that it doesn't conflict with other standalone GTK or Python instances running on the same machine.

### Steps to reproduce the bug
*   Launch portable `Nicotine+.exe`.
*   Attempt to launch another portable GTK application, for example, `zim.exe`.
*   Observe that `zim.exe` hangs in Task Manager indefinitely without displaying a window.


### Additional context:
* **Nicotine+ version:** Both current 3.3.10 builds and older versions (back when Windows 7 was fully supported).
* **OS:** Windows 7 x64 This is NOT an OS-specific deprecation issue.
* **Root cause:** Nicotine+'s single-instance implementation aggressively hijacks the generic GApplication local socket channel on Windows. Any other standalone Python/GTK application started afterwards mistakes Nicotine+'s socket for its own backend, refuses to spawn a window, and hangs as a ghost process.

*   **Workaround found:** The only way to make them work together is to force Zim Wiki into a randomized environment via a batch script using custom `XDG_*` variables and a randomized `ZIM_UNIQUE_ID`: 

bat

    set "ZIM_UNIQUE_ID=%RANDOM%%RANDOM%"
    set "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=%TEMP%\zim_rt_%ZIM_UNIQUE_ID%"
    set "XDG_CONFIG_HOME=%TEMP%\zim_cfg_%ZIM_UNIQUE_ID%"
    set "XDG_CACHE_HOME=%TEMP%\zim_cch_%ZIM_UNIQUE_ID%"
    set "XDG_DATA_HOME=%TEMP%\zim_dat_%ZIM_UNIQUE_ID%"

title: Implement plugin action system
body:
Allows plugins to specify actions, a combination of a label and callback, for presentation in the UI. The action system complements the command system, by providing a way to easily interact with a plugin without requiring the use of CLI/chat commands.

For now, only global plugin actions can be defined, which appear in a plugin action menu next to the main menu (or a Plugins submenu in the menu bar, if header bars are disabled).

In the future, contexts can be introduced, which the UI can use to show actions in specific parts of the application, e.g. as menu items for transfers or chats.

title: Select files in the opened folder
body:
### Description
`Select a file` -> `right click` -> `Open in File Manager` opens the folder containing the selected file, but it would be nice, especially for folders with lots of files, if the chosen file was automatically selected in the opened folder.

### Additional context
On Windows, this can be done by running `explorer` with the `/select` flag, e.g. `explorer /select,"C:\Windows\wininit.ini"`. This opens the folder `C:\Windows` and selects the file `wininit.ini`.

It's also possible to select multiple files in a folder, but it's more complex.
```python
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from win32com.shell import shell, shellcon

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from _win32typing import PyIDL


def open_folder_and_select_items(dirname: str, paths: list[str]) -> None:
    """
    Open a folder in Windows Explorer and select the specified items.

    Args:
        dirname: The directory to open.
        paths: A list of file paths whose basenames should be selected
            inside the opened directory.
    """
    folder_path = Path(dirname).resolve()

    # SHILCreateFromPath returns (pidl, attributes)
    folder_pidl, _ = shell.SHILCreateFromPath(
        str(folder_path),
        shellcon.SFGAO_FOLDER,
    )

    # Build PIDLs for each target file directly instead of enumerating the
    # folder contents. This is simpler and avoids pywin32 COM binding issues.
    selected: list[PyIDL] = []

    for path in paths:
        item_path = Path(path)

        # Resolve relative paths against dirname.
        if not item_path.is_absolute():
            item_path = folder_path / item_path

        if not item_path.exists():
            continue

        item_pidl, _ = shell.SHILCreateFromPath(str(item_path), 0)
        selected.append(item_pidl)

    # If an empty list is passed to SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems, Windows opens
    # the parent folder and selects the folder itself. To avoid this, pass the
    # folder PIDL itself.
    if len(selected) == 0:
        selected = [folder_pidl]

    shell.SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems(folder_pidl, tuple(selected))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    open_folder_and_select_items(r"C:\Windows", [r"C:\Windows\wininit.ini", r"C:\Windows\system.ini"])
```

title: PeerMessage: parse_virtual_path() to validate directory name components
body:
This is a draft PR intended to aid development and testing to try out if an approach to impose limits upon what names and how many files can be shared, searched and browsed at the protocol level, as to if it would be feasible and not be too restrictive.

- Removed: Don't replace forward slashes of incoming directory entries. No peer should transmit improper path separators in their shared folder listings. As a side effect of not replacing these, files that contain forward-slashes "`/`" in their names could be better supported (i.e. so they don't fracture the tree view nodes, and so that such files could be looked up by the peer).

+ Added: Validate virtual path and file name components to aim for partial UDF naming compliance when:
    - Scanning shares - to prevent from the client from sharing faulty directory listings to other peers on the network
    - Receiving search results
    - Receiving list of a folder contents from a peer
    - Receiving list of shared files from a browsed peer

+ Changed: Use unordered sets for ILLEGAL constants instead of ordered lists, because sets are immutable and hashable.

<details><summary>Restrictions imposed BOTH ways, on what cannot be listed for sharing AND what cannot be received...</summary>
    - No folder or file name that contains an illegal CTRL character IN it (names with illegal PRINTABLE chars ARE still allowed)</br>
    - No folder or file basename that is only 1 character long AND is an illegal file character</br>
    - No folder or file basename that is, or would strip down to, a relative directory path traversal identifier (ie, `.`, `..`, `~`, `/`)</br>
    - No folder or file basename that is, or would strip down to, an absolute zero-length string (ie, ` ` -> `\\`)</br>
    - No folder or file base stem that is, or would strip down to, a Windows system reserved name (ie, `NUL`, `CON.ext`, etc)</br>
    - No more than `4194304` total number of folders in a shared directory listing (silently drop entry or log scanner errors)</br>
    - No more than `65535` file entries within any single shared folder (silently drop entry or log scanner errors)</br>
    - _(todo note: there is no limit on the total number of files in all folders, suggest max count 65536*65536=`UINT32`)_</br>
</details>

<details><summary>Restrictions imposed on what cannot be listed by other peers when receiving responses FROM them...</summary>
    - No directory entry containing any single folder or file name component that is larger than 4 KiB (`4096` Bytes)</br>
    - No directory entry with a concatenated path+filename larger than a sum total of 32 KiB (`32768` Bytes)</br>
    - No directory entry containing a folder path that is nested deeper than `1024` parent levels in a shared tree listing</br>
    - _(note: above errors will result in a `__INVALID_SHARE__<>` sentinel being prepended to invalidate only that directory entry)_</br>
    - No more than `25000` search result entries in any single search response from a peer (any excess are silently dropped)</br>
</details>

<details><summary>Additional restrictions imposed on what cannot be listed for sharing out TO other peers...</summary>
    - No directory entry containing any single folder or file name component that is larger than `254` Bytes</br>
    - No directory entry with a concatenated path+filename larger than a sum total of 4 KiB (`4096` Bytes)</br>
    - No folder that is nested more than `512` levels deep in the shared directory tree listing</br>
    - No folder or file name that ends with a space or dot (` `, `.`)</br>
    - _(note: such errors will result in a logged message raised when rescanning shares, and that entry won't be shared)_</br>
</details>

Disallowing such shared directory entries is not intended to be total tyranny, since entries caught by the parser as implemented in this PR would probably lead to an unresolvable path later on, or it would not be downloadable by some other clients anyway.

This doesn't prevent illegal characters being within a name (provided that that character is not the only character in the name), so a further implementation to normalize path component names when saving files to disk would still be required as well.

UDF 1.02 is used a reference because it uses defacto standards relevant to multimedia filesystem interoperability. See link:
https://dev.ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA_TR-112-7_1st_edition_december_2023.pdf

title: utils.py: truncate with CRC suffix for UDF compliant path name component
body:
+ Added: Standard truncation algorithm that could be used to avoid the risk of filename collisions when renaming path or file name components that are too long or contain illegal characters.

Note I used AI to help me write the `crc_hqx()` hex calculation on line 319, so I'm not sure if the generated characters are mathematically correct since I do not understand how the heck that bit works exactly.

Based on the rules specified in "ECMA TR/112-7 Universal Disk Format (UDF) specification – Part 7 (Revision 1.02)"...
Section 4.2.2.1.2 "OS/2 FileIdentifier" step 5 (page 64) and the  CRC Calculation in appendix 6.5, at link:
https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA_TR-112-7_1st_edition_december_2023.pdf

> **Universal Disk Format Revision 1.02 Part 7 (Revision 1.02) Section 4**
> User Interface Requirements - File System
> 
> **Definitions**:
> A _FileIdentifier_ shall be considered as being composed of two parts, a file
> name and file extension.
> 
> The character '.' (`#002E`) shall be considered as the separator for the
> FileIdentifier of a file; characters appearing subsequent to the last '.'
> (`#002E`) shall be considered as constituting the file extension if and only if
> it is less than or equal to 5 characters in length, otherwise the file
> extension shall not exist. Characters appearing prior to the file extension,
> excluding the last '.' (`#002E`), shall be considered as constituting the file
> name.
> 
> **NOTE**: Even though OS/2 , Macintosh , and UNIX do not have an
> official concept of a filename extension it is common file naming
> conventions to end a file with “.” followed by a 1 to 5 character
> extension. Therefore the following algorithms attempt to preserve
> the file extension up to a maximum of 5 characters.
> 
> ...
> 5. **FileIdentifier CRC**: Since through the above process character
> information from the original FileIdentifier is lost the chance of
> creating a duplicate FileIdentifier in the same directory
> increases. To greatly reduce the chance of having a duplicate
> FileIdentifier the file name shall be modified to contain a CRC of
> the original FileIdentifier.
> 
> If there is a file extension then the new FileIdentifier shall be
> composed of up to the first (254 - (length of (new file extension) + 1 
> (for the '.')) - 4 (for the #CRC)) characters constituting the
> file name at this step in the process, followed by the separator
> '#' (`#0023`); followed by a 3 digit CS0 Hex representation of the
> least significant 12 bits of the 16-bit CRC of the original CS0
> FileIdentifier, followed by '.' (`#002E`) and the file extension at
> this step in the process.
> 
> Otherwise if there is no file extension the new FileIdentifier shall
> be composed of up to the first (254 - 4 (for the #CRC))
> characters constituting the file name at this step in the process.
> Followed by the separator '#' (`#0023`); followed by a 3 digit CS0
> Hex representation of the least significant 12 bits of the 16-bit
> CRC of the original CS0 FileIdentifier.

_Note: The above text is from a 2023 revision but hasn't changed much since the original 1998 version of this document._

It is (was) most commonly used to burn files onto Compact Discs and DVD's, but several embedded filesystems such as used on many MP3 players apparently also implement this same algorithm, as far as I can tell, is or was also similar to that used by old or current Windows FAT and NTFS filesystems (with the exception of the legacy character encoding) after IBM's version of HPFS support was merged in the early NT kernels (~before~ in NT4 ~or maybe even since before NT3.51~).

https://ss64.com/nt/syntax-filenames.html

```
slsk://alias/Articles/internet_protocols/kademlia/maymounkov-kademlia-lncs.pdf?tr=server.slsknet.org:2242&xl=215911
```

```
magnet:?xs=slsk://alias/pathname&tr=server.slsknet.org:2242&ws=https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/~petar/papers/maymounkov-kademlia-lncs.pdf&xl=215911
```

title: uploads.py: differentiate 'started' vs 'resumed' uploads
body:
@mathiascode This is just an idea I haven't tested properly. Basically I think it will help if we could somehow identify when an upload is resumed vs started from the beginning.

I think the Transfer() object already contains most data we would need to identify if a non-compliant peer never got the beginning of a file (that's assuming auto-clear uploads list isn't enabled) and just went in for a chunk.

So it's just a matter of presenting a warning in the interface or at least in the log so we start investigating what action should be taken to gracefully handle this kind of scenario (like not sending the speed nor incrementing the stats unless it's known that all of the entire file bytes had actually been transferred).

+ Added: Identify resumed uploads in the transfer logs

Draft PR, not for merge.

title: Allocate upload slots feature efficiency
body:
Nicotine+ version: 3.3.10
Operating System/Distribution: Linux/Flatpak


### Describe the bug
My uploading setup is as follows: "round robin" and "allocate upload slots until total speed reaches 50kbps". It works as expected until there's only one upload left, once that upload finishes Nicotine seems to open too many upload slots, for example I just observed it open 5 slots for uploading which means everyone is downloading very slowly now. On a fast connection this isn't much of an issue, but on slow one it means uploads will slow down to double digits.

### Expected behavior
Staggered or delayed opening of new slots. Once that last download finishes, it should wait until opening new slots until the upload speed reaches 50kbps (or whatever I choose to set in the options)

### Steps to reproduce the bug
1. Set the upload queue type to round robin
2. Set allocate upload slots until total speed reaches to 50kbps, or possibly lower to trigger the bug more easily
3. Wait for multiple people to queue files from you
4. Wait for an upload to finish while you only have one file uploading
5. Now multiple upload slots should instantly open

title: Adding Structure to Downloads
body:
# General Suggestion: 
I am hoping to find a way to add structure to downloads when not downloading full folders.

I imagine a lot of users also use beets or similar programs to sort files after downloading so increased file sorting helps beets mass sort files.

# Pathway Description
In SoulSeekQT downloads follow the following structure regardless of if I download the full folder from a user.
`Complete > User > Album/Folder Name > Files`

But in Nicotine+ the structure is

title: Feature Request: Add IPv6 support
body:
Hey team,

A lot of us are stuck behind ISPs that use CGNAT or just flat-out block port forwarding. This means we can't be "connectable" on Soulseek, so no one can browse our files or download from us, which really limits our ability to share.

Adding full IPv6 support would fix this problem for good.

With IPv6, everyone gets their own unique public IP address. There's no more NAT, and no more need to mess with port forwarding. We'd just be connectable, straight up.

**Why this would be great:**

* Solves many connectivity problem: Anyone on CGNAT or with a fussy ISP could finally be connectable.

* Faster, more stable connections: Direct end-to-end connections are just better and have less latency than trying to punch through a NAT.

* A healthier network: More connectable users = more available files for everyone.

* Future-proof: More and more of the internet (especially mobile networks) is moving to IPv6.

This seems like the best long-term solution, since IPv4 and CGNAT issues are only going to get more common.

Thanks for considering it!

title: Reverse share scanning order (Trusted, Buddy, Public) to better handle nested shares
body:
As pointed out by @slook in https://github.com/nicotine-plus/nicotine-plus/issues/3496#issuecomment-3513919218

Currently shares are scanned in order: Public, Buddy, Trusted.
This results in (nested) Trusted/Buddy shares being shared as if they were Buddy/Public shares.
Reversing the scanning order should exclude them from shares of lower trust, as the directories would already be scanned.

Additional suggestion: adding Private (or Exclude, or any other term) scanned before Trusted would create an easy way for creating completely private directories, and exempt them from sharing.

I believe this set needs to be reversed:
https://github.com/nicotine-plus/nicotine-plus/blob/master/pynicotine/shares.py#L303-L309

I would be happy if someone more familiar with the code could look into it, in case the behaviour change would require more code changes.

title: Use os.fsencode() and os.fsdecode() for pathlike byte strings

Closes #3485 (possibly - testing todo)

- https://peps.python.org/pep-0519/ "Adding a file system path protocol" (Python-Version: 3.6)
_" If a str is desired and the encoding of bytes should be assumed to be the default file system encoding, then [os.fsdecode()](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.fsdecode) should be used."_

- https://peps.python.org/pep-0529/ "Change Windows filesystem encoding to UTF-8" (Python-Version: 3.6)
_"On Windows bytes cannot round-trip all characters used in paths, as Python internally uses the *A functions and hence the encoding is “whatever the active code page is”. Since the active code page cannot represent all Unicode characters, the conversion of a path into bytes can lose information without warning or any available indication."_

- https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.getfilesystemencoding
_"[os.fsencode()](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.fsencode) and [os.fsdecode()](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.fsdecode) should be used to ensure that the correct encoding and errors mode are used."_

title: Soulseek / Nicotine the Next Generation - Hash driven goodness
body:
Feature request / discussion as to whether it's got legs.

Idea:
Nicotine generates a SHA256 hash for every shared file (perhaps on opt in basis). Users can search by hash.

This opens up a world of possibility for collaborative vetting of files by the community since you can uniquely identify any file by its hash.

- Compile a database of the perfect CDrip of every track, identified by hash.
- Look up what is considered the perfect rip of the best vinyl version of a track - again the discussion is possible because everyone can agree on what they're talking about based on the hash.

Down the road, this opens up more possibilities:

- People can share tracklistings for an album, identified by hashes. Want to pull a particular or 'best' version of the album, search the tracklisting that has been agreed as best by the community, identified by it's hash, then pull the individual tracks by their hash,
-  Possibility to automatically pull an album given its tracklisting. Tracks could be pulled from multiple users- this combines a lot of the advantages of both Soulseek sharing model and torrent.
- Integrity can be checked by recalculating hash and checking it against the listed one.
- Corrupted copies could be identified by clients messaging the originator.

I realise there's a lot here and some will probably need Soulseek server side involvement, but what Nicotine+ could do as a starter and to float the idea is:
- Perform hashing
- Create and share hash tables

It certainly needs some thought, there are limits as to what Nicotine can achieve alone and there are possible limitations - for example these hashes could take a long while to calculate.. possible workaround calculate in background and make available as and when.

I think this is worth some thought and could be an audiophile dream - but whether it's something for Nicotine, well I'm interested to know what the devs think.

I would throw £100 if you start a kickstarter and I think you could start with some fairly simple / focused functionality.

P.S. I know flac files already contain a checksum / fingerprint. Might not be quite as unique (hash length) as SHA256 but probably 'good enough' for the use case of this particular file type.

title: Use OR and AND and "Quotes" for advanced filtering using Include text and Exclude text fields
body:
### Describe the solution you'd like
When using the "Include text" and "Exclude text" fields with space-separated terms, it appears that the search filter treats it as a single string literal, when I'd expect it to treat multiple words as "AND". 

Example:

If I search for "House of the Dragon" then use **Include text** to filter to "S01", it works as expected. If I use "S01 Prince" (to narrow it down to the episode "The Rogue Prince" in Season 1) it does NOT work, as it's filtering to the literal string "S01 Prince" instead of searching for results that include both "S01" AND "Prince". This is the functionality I would expect if I had put quote marks around S01 Prince.

Another example:

If I search for "The Social Network" and I'm looking for the movie and not the soundtrack, I might want to use **Exclude text** to filter out audio files. I would expect to be able to type in "mp3 ogg flac" so that it filters out any instances of the terms "mp3" OR "ogg" OR "flac", but again it is searching for that entire literal string to filter out.

Alternatively the & symbol could be substituted for AND, and the | symbol substituted for OR, if it is determined it would be better to utilize special symbols for this functionality.

Note: The official Soulseek client's filter works by treating each individual term as if separated by AND, and a "-" symbol before as "Exclude", all in a single field. I do like having separate fields in Nicotine+, but do not like that they are treated as string literals.

title: ChatView: infinite read back scrolling
body:
After this concept is reviewed/tested in principle, the intent is break this draft PR into multiple smaller PRs.

+ Added: Clickable `roomname` tags to close #2482
+ Added: Infinite scrolling in chat views with memory-efficient buffering to read back log files
+ Removed: "readroomlines" and "readprivatelines" config settings
+ Changed: Prepend chat logs into ChatView widgets upon tab activation rather than during application launch
+ Fixed: Part of the timestamp was incorrectly tagged if the username is a short numeric that's also in timestamp
+ Fixed: New room wall message was appended at the end instead of being prepended to start upon text entry
+ Avoids the use of `find()` when inserting text for online chat messages, it is only needed when reading old log file lines

- Reverts `msg.formatted_message` since this direct tag insertion approach doesn't require it.

The idea of tagging entire lines together in a list of `(text, tag),` tuples is for the purpose of an on-demand log file readback mechanism. Reading backwards is not possible otherwise, because the text elements would be inserted out of order.

Not only is application startup time much improved when lots of lines need to be read from many logs, but the ability to prepend old `read_log_lines` into ChatView provides scope for infinitely reading back old messages from the log file on demand, even after new chat message lines have already been appended, since the `last_read_line` number within the file can be known at the startup datum, and thereafter be tracked (by keeping a reference to it in the `LogFile` object) upon every scroll-up/page-up event, until the Beginning Of File is reached.

Reading lines from a log file into a buffer is a trivial operation that is relatively fast, yet the slowest part of the operation is tagging and rendering formatted hypertext into the widget. Hence, these slow operations can be postponed indefinitely until the tab is activated, and more data only needs to read when scrolling up is actually occurring.

Reference draft PR #2540

title: core_commands: split lexical arguments with shlex
body:
+ Added: Accept "long strings with spaces" as quoted arguments, but don't require quotes if arguments are unambiguous
+ Added: Support long "user names" with spaces for the `/msg` and `/usearch` commands
+ Added: Support long "room names" with spaces for the `/say` command
+ Added: A third argument in the `/sample` command to test this implementation with 3 arguments

Lexical (shell-like) argument splitting allows support for quoted "user names". Quotes are not mandatory if the argument is the first or last one, nor if the username is a single word, i.e; the following inputs all validate into 2 arguments:

`/msg "user name" "message text"`  <- both arguments quoted, ok.
`/msg user name "message text"`  <- only final argument quoted, ok.
`/msg "user name" message text`  <- only first argument quoted, ok.
`/msg username message text`  <- no quotes required for single-word usernames, ok.

_Review/testing points:_

- 3 or more `num_required_args` are tested working with the new `split_args()` function. The `/msg` only needs to accept two arguments, but other commands might need more.

- Only un-quoted arguments will be split. Quoted arguments are always protected from splitting. A helpful error message is shown on the interface in the case of a mismatch, such as "Too many arguments".

- Setting `num_required_args=0` returns unlimited splits, and thus will split all un-quoted arguments as separate words, as per the standard split function without _maxsplit_, or _maxsplit=-1_, but the quoted phrases will be together as one argument.

- It is very likely that the `<user>` argument will contain spaces, because many users have such long names. Some commands, such as `/usearch` for example) are useless without support for arguments that contain spaces.

- The proposed implementation is a useful utility that should be available to plugin developers to process any string in the way they want, with any amount of required arguments (such as perhaps from secondary input() prompt or another source).

- Closer integration for argument parsing might be considered into the pluginsystem core, but caution is needed to ensure that optional arguments don't throw an error that prevents the plugin command from being triggered.

- If there is a combination of required arguments plus two or more optional arguments then arguments can be ambiguous, but having one optional argument (such as in most private chat commands) in the final position would be okay.

- Strings containing `'`_inline `"`quotes`"` can be `"`protected`"` with alternate quotation marks_`'`, and other features, but unfortunately there is no _maxsplit_ feature, which is why we need to extend the shlex function such as done in this PR.
 
See [shlex module Python docs](https://docs.python.org/3.8/library/shlex.html#shlex.split) for details.

It would be nice if the installer registered the `slsk://` URL protocol on Windows, something like [this](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/80650/how-do-i-register-a-custom-url-protocol-in-windows), or how qBittorrent handles magnet links on Windows:
```
﻿Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\slsk]
"URL Protocol"=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\slsk\shell]

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\slsk\shell\open]

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\slsk\shell\open\command]
@="\"E:\\Program Files\\pf(x64\\Nicotine+\\Nicotine+.exe\" \"%1\""
```

### Additional context
It would also be nice if the installer would pick up previous installations of Nicotine+, instead of defaulting to `C:\Program Files\Nicotine+\` every time.

title: Remember the File Search Results column layout for each Result Grouping Mode (GtkTreeView)
body:
### Describe the problem
File Search Results column widths+order layout settings are not appropriately remembered in the GtkTreeView widget, so the user must constantly adjust the view layout per search tab depending upon the current Result Grouping Mode and main window size, factors... which are of course constantly changing.

It is highly frustrating after having adjusted the column widths and column order, that these layout settings are not synchronized across other child search tabs that have the same Result Grouping Mode.

If a user wishes to refine the customization of their column widths and order, then they are only able to do so reliably when only one search tab is open, because closing the tabs in the incorrect order will wipe out the changed width+order settings, with only the last open tab's settings remembered, and it's too easy to forget what's what so it's basically a lottery.

### Describe the solution you'd like
What would perhaps seem to make more sense, is associating the column width+order settings for each of the three defined Result Grouping Mode's, so that any changes are synchronized across all open and future search tabs.

- So basically there needs to be three **persistent** user-customizable column layouts:
1. GtkTreeView layout settings for **Ungrouped**
2. GtkTreeView layout settings for **Group by Folder**
3. GtkTreeView layout settings for **Group by User**

- Then, the chosen settings will be remembered forever until another adjustment is made by the user.

title: Album/Folder Level Result Filters
body:
Add result filters that match for the whole folder instead of file level:
Minimum Matching Files: Only shows results for folders that have at least X number of files that match the file type filter. So if a folder has 20 images but only one song that matches, filter out the folder.
Maximum Matching Files: Only shows results for folders that have at most X number of files that match the file type filter. So if an album has multiple rereleases you can filter out the rereleases easier.
Contains: Only show results for folders that have at least one file that matches text or !text. Ex. Main Search term "Animal Tracks" with Folder Filter Contains "Mess Around" would show results matching for https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Tracks_(British_album)
